source.title: Long-Tail Theory under Gaussian Mixtures
source.authors: A. Bolatov; Maxat Tezekbayev; Igor Melnykov; Artur Pak; Vassilina Nikoulina; Z. Assylbekov

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether removing highly memorized training examples changes held-out error, using an approximate memorization score and SST-2 sentiment classification.
record.gate_note: The paper discusses benign overfitting and cites results from other work, but those are not this study’s results. The synthetic LDA/MDA experiments do not test the listed claim versions. The SST-2 experiment reports test-error curves for models trained after removing top-memorized examples; exact values are figure-only, and no random-removal comparison is reported.
record.test_reason: The SST-2 experiment tests the absolute accuracy effect of removing highly memorized examples in a new setting. It bears on V8, but lacks the random-removal control needed to establish V8's comparative effect.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the SST-2 conclusion. More broadly, the authors establish a Gaussian-mixture setting where MDA can fit rare subpopulations and outperform LDA, and report synthetic and SST-2 results consistent with a narrowing gap as the tail shortens. They acknowledge that high-removal deterioration falls outside their theory and that their theoretical analysis does not establish benign overfitting.
record.recipe_differences: Uses an approximate memorization score rather than retraining for each example to calculate the score; removes selected examples and retrains sentiment classifiers on SST-2.
record.method_sensitivity: The error gap becomes statistically non-significant at high removal percentages, where examples from main subpopulations are also removed and both classifiers’ performance sharply worsens.

fits_no_version.finding: Linear has higher test error than DNN, and their gap slightly decreases as highly memorized examples are removed.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: On SST-2, the advantage of finetuning DistilBERT over a frozen-representation linear classifier narrows slightly after removing highly memorized training examples.

fits_no_version.finding: Gaussian-mixture theory and synthetic experiments show an advantage for MDA over LDA when rare subpopulations are present.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under the specified Gaussian-mixture distribution, fitting minority subpopulations can improve generalization over a misspecified linear classifier.

fits_no_version.finding: Overparameterized MDA reaches zero training error for almost all tested component-count pairs and can retain favorable test performance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign interpolation can occur with redundant Gaussian-mixture components, with performance depending on the balance of components across classes.

record.problems: The real-data experiment approximates the memorization score; there is no random-removal comparison. Figure 9 reports curves without exact values in the supplied text. The authors note that high removal percentages affect main subpopulations and are outside their theory.
record.rows_left_out: No other results bear on the listed versions. Synthetic LDA/MDA results and overparameterized MDA results concern classifiers on the authors’ Gaussian-mixture setup, not the mapped conditions for V1–V8.

untested.parts: Fixed random-label fitting and natural-label versus random-label held-out performance.
Network widening beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under comparable tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps.
Whether removing highly memorized examples hurts accuracy more than removing equally many random examples; the image-classification and MNIST comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: No verdict label is justified for V8's comparison with random removal. The stated high-removal deterioration supports its absolute-removal component, but the missing control is an untested component, not evidence limiting or challenging the claim. Figure 9's numerical curves are unavailable in the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: No width sweep of one-hidden-layer ReLU networks.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No adaptive-optimizer versus SGD generalization comparison.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or other generalization-measure comparison.
Tests removal of top-memorized examples, but does not compare against removing the same number of random examples; exact curve values are not stated in text.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: The study removes highly memorized training examples, retrains classifiers and measures held-out error, providing results bearing on V8.

tranche.reason: The SST-2 removal experiment extends the question to sentiment classification with pretrained Distill-BERT. It reports deterioration at high removal fractions, but lacks the random-removal control required to determine V8's comparative effect.

source_check.notes: The DNN has 66 million parameters; the study provides no controlled parameter-scaling comparison. Figure 9 supplies no exact error values in the extracted text; confidence bands cover averages across nine runs.
